title: Aviyan Pandey
text:
Aviyan Pandey is a PhD student in the Department of Soil and Crop Sciences at Colorado State University, advised by Dr. Meagan Schipanski.
Tracing how plants, roots, and microbes move carbon and nitrogen through agroecosystems.


My research focuses on soil carbon and nitrogen cycling in agroecosystems. I use microbial biomass and enzyme activity measurements, ¹³C/¹⁵N isotope tracing, and root trait variation to understand plant–soil–microbe interactions under climate warming, nutrient management, and water limitation. My current work spans bioenergy and forage crops (switchgrass, sorghum) and cover crop residue dynamics, with a growing interest in connecting field and greenhouse measurements to soil organic matter modeling.

How warming and N fertilization interact to shape soil respiration and microbial function in a switchgrass system, with a planned multi-year extension.
Sorghum genotype × water × nitrogen limitation | Colorado State University
NIFA-funded field and greenhouse work on how genotype, water, and N limitation shape root traits and soil processes.
Cover crop litter quality and C/N cycling | Colorado State University
Greenhouse pot study (co-authored) on how cover crop litter quality affects C and N cycling with growing corn.
MEMS 2.0 site build, Akron, CO | Colorado State University
Building a new MEMS 2.0 site to model soil organic matter dynamics.
